cases.name: Linda Sue Hanoian Peterson
cases.about: She was a nurse at the University of Utah.
cases.caseStatus: COLD CASE UNSOLVED; MISSING PERSON CASE
cases.narrative:
On 9/30/1978, her husband, William “Phil” Peterson reported her missing. Phil reported to Murray Police Linda had stopped by his work, Grand Central located at 750 East 2100 South, on September 16, 1978.

Phil was working at this location as a pharmacist; Phil stated that Linda had entered through the back employee doors to speak with him. Phil stated that Linda planned a last-minute trip to Kentucky with two “girlfriends”. Phil stated that he did not know the females but believes one of their names was Susan. Phil stated that he provided Linda with $300 in cash (2025 currency $1,500) and noted that Linda had her master card with her. It was reported that Linda left in a station wagon of an unknown color and unknown plate number. The credit card was never used after Linda’s disappearance. Phil passed away in 2013; only limited statements from Phil are available. 

At the time Linda went missing she was 5 1/2 months pregnant. Due to other miscarriages that Linda had suffered she had put herself on bedrest. Linda’s mother, Irene, reported that the week Linda went missing she was sending Linda furniture, and that Linda would have not left town when such a large delivery was going to be made. Irene stated that she was in weekly contact with Linda and that is was completely out of character for Linda to stop communicating with Irene. Irene passed away a few years later without ever having contact from Linda again. 

Detectives later discovered that Linda had lived in Kentucky, years prior to her going missing, and that she had only lived there for about four months. Linda no longer had friends in the area and there was no reason for Linda to visit Kentucky. There isn’t any supporting evidence that Linda left the state of Utah. It should also be noted that the two females Linda was reported to be with were never reported missing or identified. 

Linda has living family members that are still actively searching for her. Due to Linda being adopted at birth it wasn’t until 2025 that family DNA could be collected.

cases.name: Jamie Lynn Taylor Salazar
cases.about:
"More than anything, Jamie was a mother," her sister Melissa Gilham said.

"She was the kind of mother who took walks, played on the swings, did finger paints, hand sewed costumes, made beautiful homemade wall art for their walls, had snowball fights, snuggled on the couch watching movies, and said prayers every night. And she took pics of every step. Jamie was a friend to everyone she ever met. There isn't a person who met her who didn't love her," she recalled fondly.

Gilham said her tender hearted sister "wouldn't even let me squish a spider." She described her as a woman who "had 500 pairs of shoes," but preferred to go barefoot. Her friends also said she was a talented photographer.

cases.name: Carol Kay Jones Durkes
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Carol was a beloved, selfless, caring, understanding mother, daughter, aunt, and friend. Her interests were many, and she was known as an amateur photographer, a passionate car-singer, professional penny pincher, and lifelong dog lover. She was an established seamstress and antique collector and restorer. She loved game night with her kids and neighbors as well as building puzzles, skiing, hiking, traveling, and sightseeing. She enjoyed planning all the details for future vacations and trips which was fueled by her sense of adventure and excitement to experience the world. She didn’t wait for “someday.” She exuded genuine warmth and compassion, and an absolute zest for life. She cherished her children and family dearly. She was as beautiful on the inside as she was on the outside."
cases.narrative: She had obvious signs of trauma to her body.

cases.name: Morgan Kay Harris
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Morgan grew up in Cedar City, Ut. where she did well in school, danced, played volleyball, played piano and enjoyed reading, ceramics, and baking. She was a professional model for a couple of years. She became disenchanted with the pressure to remain very thin by people in the industry. She married Cody Harris in 2013.They moved to New Orleans, LA while he was in the military. While married, she enjoyed redecorating their home and doing sewing and craft projects. She really wanted to be a mom, but was never able to carry a full term baby. After many fertility treatments and miscarriages, she re-focused her love and energy on their dogs and her nieces and nephews. She built a close relationship with her mother-in-law, Jamie DeMille, who has also passed. She divorced after moving to Ogden, Ut.. She became a medical assistant and enjoyed helping with medical research trials.

Morgan spent the rest of her life in northern Utah with her dog Huck. She spent a lot of time with her sisters and made time for her nieces and nephews. Morgan is described as shy and the most gentle, kind, peace-making soul by everyone who knew her. She was artistic, liked to be informed on current issues, thought deeply and conversed about many subjects."
cases.narrative: He allegedly locked her and her dog in a storage unit before it caught fire.
